newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AWB Report-Australian prices still up on weather.
newsitem.headline: AWB Report-Australian prices still up on weather.

text.p: The Australian Wheat Board's (AWB) national indicator price hit a high of A$196 a tonne fob in the latest week on continuing concern over world weather, intially in the U.S. and Europe, the Australian Wheat Board (AWB) said in its weekly report.
New crop values have been stronger with higher U.S. futures prices attributed to U.S. flooding and frost damage and European dryness, AWB said.
Around Australia no significant rainfall was recorded, with Western Australia the only state with significant subsoil moisture, it said.
The window for rain was becoming narrower with growers needing a break to plant in the next month or so to have any assurance that the crop would not be affected, it said.

Some take-up of multigrade indicator price contract sales to the AWB by farmers had occurred but a reluctance by growers to sign fixed grade contracts, especially for higher protein wheat or riskier grains, was evident, it said.
The old crop stock feed sector continued to move higher especially for barley, wheat and triticale as an absence of a break in the weather brought a lack of grower selling, it said.
